title: California Shines a Spotlight on Disability Pride Month with Statewide Proclamation - NewsBreak
text: Sacramento, California – Acting Governor Eleni Kounalakis has officially declared July 2025 as Disability Pride Month in California, spotlighting the Golden State’s commitment to accessibility and inclusion. The proclamation, issued from the state capital on July 8, encourages Californians to honor the contributions and rights of people with disabilities throughout the month. Kounalakis’ announcement from Sacramento comes with historical weight. Disability Pride Month is observed nationwide each July to commemorate the passage of the Americans with Disabilities Act. According to the proclamation, the legislation, signed on July 26, 1990, was "a major civil rights milestone" that banned discrimination against people with disabilities in areas such as public transportation, employment, and education. It was spearheaded by California’s own Congressman Tony Coelho, the proclamation noted. "California joins communities around the nation in recognizing July as Disability Pride Month, an opportunity to celebrate the many ways that people living with disabilities – whether visible or invisible, mobility or cognitive, vision or hearing, learning or sensory, developmental or acquired – add to the diversity and strength of our state," Acting Governor Kounalakis stated in the proclamation. The statement emphasized that California is home to more than 7 million adults living with disabilities and serves one in eight children with disability-related services in schools. From Sacramento to San Diego, and across cities like Fresno, Stockton, and Los Angeles, the proclamation highlights the diverse efforts across the state to promote inclusion. Kounalakis underscored the work of the Newsom Administration and the Legislature in advancing civil rights and increasing access to education, employment, health care, and independent living for people with disabilities. "The state also continues to prioritize accessibility of all state services and is deepening our commitment to employment opportunities for people with disabilities within state service," she stated. She called on residents to reflect on the significance of Disability Pride Month, saying, "As we celebrate Disability Pride Month, let us reflect on the essential contributions of people with disabilities to our communities, our state, and our nation, and reaffirm our commitment to their rights and independence."
